Sell My House Fast in Houston, TX: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Texas
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Sell Your Houston House for Cash

Tell us about your Houston house. We buy as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from the Texas statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

A Houston homeowner who wants to sell can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer. Each route has different costs and timelines under Texas law, and this guide lays them out with official sources. Houston had an estimated 2,397,315 residents in 2025, and the Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $253,400 in its 2019-2023 survey. We did not use listing-site price data.

Houston housing at a glance

These figures come from the Census Bureau. They describe the city as a whole, not your street or your house. Houston sits in more than one county: Fort Bend County, Harris County, Montgomery County and Waller County. Which county tax office you deal with depends on where the house is.

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 2,397,315 (Census Bureau).
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $253,400 (American Community Survey, 2019-2023).
  • Owner-occupied homes: 384,672. Renter-occupied homes: 531,864, so about 42% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.
  • Median gross rent: $1,313 a month.
  • Median year homes were built: 1981.
  • Vacant housing units: 106,576 of 1,023,112 total.

Three ways to sell a house in Houston

List with an agent. Texas does not set commission rates. TREC says it does not regulate the fees paid to license holders, and its resale contract says compensation is fully negotiable. You also pick up closing costs, repairs and showings. See Texas real estate commission and closing costs.

Sell it yourself. A seller of a residential property with no more than one dwelling unit generally has to give the buyer the Seller's Disclosure Notice, and a lien disclosure if a recorded lien will remain at closing. Details are in for sale by owner in Texas.

Take a cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs charged to you. You choose the closing date, and the title company pays any mortgage and unpaid property tax from the proceeds.

Selling in Houston?
We buy Houston houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Situations we see with Houston houses

Behind on the mortgage. A Texas foreclosure needs a 20-day cure notice and a 21-day notice of sale, and the sale is held on the first Tuesday of a month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. (Property Code Sec. 51.002). Read the Texas foreclosure process before you decide.

Inherited house. Who can sell depends on whether there is a will and whether the estate went through probate. See probate, affidavit of heirship and transfer on death deeds.

Unpaid property tax. Texas property tax is due January 31 and penalty and interest grow each month after that. See the Texas property tax guide and tax deed sales.

Tenants or squatters. Eviction and squatter cases follow different Texas rules.

Property tax when you sell in Houston

The Texas Comptroller says Texas has no state property tax. A county appraisal district sets your value, and each local taxing unit (the county, a school district, and sometimes a city or special district) adopts its own rate. We did not find an official source that gives one tax rate for all of Houston, so we do not state one. Ask the tax office for the amount due in the month you expect to close, and give that figure to the title company.

Homeowners can lower the bill with a homestead exemption or an appraisal protest. See also our Texas county property tax guides.

How to sell a house in Texas when you are in Houston

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded document that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Texas.

What a cash sale of a Houston house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Houston.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Texas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Houston

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Texas change, so confirm details with the official office or a Texas attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Houston

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Selling a house in Houston FAQ

Can I sell my Houston house as-is?

Yes. Texas law does not require a seller to make repairs before listing, though the Seller's Disclosure Notice requires you to state what you know about the property's condition. A cash buyer purchases as-is.

How much is a house worth in Houston?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Houston at $253,400. Your house will differ, so get a written offer or an appraisal.

Do I pay a commission to sell for cash to you?

No. Our offers carry no agent commission, fees or closing costs to you.

Can I sell a Houston house with a mortgage or unpaid taxes?

Yes. The title company pays the mortgage payoff and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds at closing.

Does Texas have a state property tax?

No. The Texas Comptroller says local taxing units set rates and collect property tax.

Tell us about your Denton house. We buy as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326

Selling a house in Denton, Texas comes down to a choice between listing it, selling it yourself and taking a cash offer. Each route has different costs and timelines under Texas law, and this guide lays them out with official sources. Denton had an estimated 169,431 residents in 2025, and the Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $325,700 in its 2019-2023 survey. We did not use listing-site price data.

Denton housing at a glance

These figures come from the Census Bureau. They describe the city as a whole, not your street or your house. Denton is in Denton County.

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 169,431 (Census Bureau).
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $325,700 (American Community Survey, 2019-2023).
  • Owner-occupied homes: 26,544. Renter-occupied homes: 27,439, so about 49% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.
  • Median gross rent: $1,344 a month.
  • Median year homes were built: 1995.
  • Vacant housing units: 3,841 of 57,824 total.

Three ways to sell a house in Denton

List with an agent. Texas does not set commission rates. TREC says it does not regulate the fees paid to license holders, and its resale contract says compensation is fully negotiable. You also pick up closing costs, repairs and showings. See Texas real estate commission and closing costs.

Sell it yourself. A seller of a residential property with no more than one dwelling unit generally has to give the buyer the Seller's Disclosure Notice, and a lien disclosure if a recorded lien will remain at closing. Details are in for sale by owner in Texas.

Take a cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs charged to you. You choose the closing date, and the title company pays any mortgage and unpaid property tax from the proceeds.

Selling in Denton?
We buy Denton houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Situations we see with Denton houses

Behind on the mortgage. A Texas foreclosure needs a 20-day cure notice and a 21-day notice of sale, and the sale is held on the first Tuesday of a month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. (Property Code Sec. 51.002). Read the Texas foreclosure process before you decide.

Inherited house. Who can sell depends on whether there is a will and whether the estate went through probate. See probate, affidavit of heirship and transfer on death deeds.

Unpaid property tax. Texas property tax is due January 31 and penalty and interest grow each month after that. See the Texas property tax guide and tax deed sales.

Tenants or squatters. Eviction and squatter cases follow different Texas rules.

Property tax when you sell in Denton

The Texas Comptroller says Texas has no state property tax. A county appraisal district sets your value, and each local taxing unit (the county, a school district, and sometimes a city or special district) adopts its own rate. We did not find an official source that gives one tax rate for all of Denton, so we do not state one. Ask the tax office for the amount due in the month you expect to close, and give that figure to the title company.

Homeowners can lower the bill with a homestead exemption or an appraisal protest. See also our Texas county property tax guides.

How to sell a house in Texas when you are in Denton

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded document that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Texas.

What a cash sale of a Denton house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Denton.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Texas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Denton

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Texas change, so confirm details with the official office or a Texas attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Denton

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Selling a house in Denton FAQ

Can I sell my Denton house as-is?

Yes. Texas law does not require a seller to make repairs before listing, though the Seller's Disclosure Notice requires you to state what you know about the property's condition. A cash buyer purchases as-is.

How much is a house worth in Denton?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Denton at $325,700. Your house will differ, so get a written offer or an appraisal.

Do I pay a commission to sell for cash to you?

No. Our offers carry no agent commission, fees or closing costs to you.

Can I sell a Denton house with a mortgage or unpaid taxes?

Yes. The title company pays the mortgage payoff and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds at closing.

Does Texas have a state property tax?

No. The Texas Comptroller says local taxing units set rates and collect property tax.
